Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $36 million class fund distributed automatically using Brightline’s member and payment records, with no claims requirement or return of unclaimed funds to Brightline. This represents a substantial discount from disputed charges while providing certainty and avoiding years of litigation for both sides. Fees and expenses would be paid separately, subject to court approval; Brightline may oppose the request, and any amount not awarded would augment the class fund. We welcome a substantive counterproposal focused on actual class recovery.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that automatic distribution using existing records is appropriate and that any court-disallowed fees should augment class recovery. Your valuation does not sufficiently account for the unresolved certification and merits issues or the delay and expense of continued litigation. We counter with a $25 million class fund and $3 million for court-approved fees and expenses, without clear sailing. Distribution and administration expenses would be included within the class fund, with no additional payment obligation; counsel’s expenses would be included within the fee amount. No unclaimed class funds would revert to Brightline; residual funds would be handled through a court-approved process benefiting the class. This provides meaningful recovery without a claims barrier.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate agreement on automatic payments, nonreversion, and independent fee review. Certification risk warrants a discount, but the surviving claims and readily identifiable renewal charges support a higher class recovery. We counter at a $32 million class fund and accept your $3 million ceiling for court-approved fees and counsel’s expenses, without clear sailing. Reasonable, documented distribution and administration costs may come from the class fund, subject to court approval and an advance budget disclosed to both sides. There would be no claims requirement and no reversion of unclaimed class funds to Brightline; residuals would first support further distributions where economically feasible, with any remaining balance handled through a court-approved process benefiting the class. Any unawarded fees would augment the class fund.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Your movement is constructive. We accept the proposed administration safeguards, including reasonable documented costs, court approval, and an advance budget disclosed to both sides, as well as the residual-distribution sequence. Certification and ultimate recovery remain uncertain, however, and settlement provides payment substantially sooner than trial. We propose a $27 million class fund plus up to $3 million for court-approved fees and counsel’s expenses. Brightline’s aggregate payment obligation would not exceed $30 million, with all notice, distribution, administration, and other settlement costs included within those amounts. Payments would be automatic, with no class-fund reversion to Brightline; any unawarded fees would augment the class fund. Brightline would retain its right to oppose the fee request. This increases our class-fund offer by $2 million while preserving the protections on which we agree.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate the increased offer and agreement on administration safeguards. To narrow the remaining gap, we propose a $30 million class fund plus $3 million for court-approved fees and counsel’s expenses, for a total commitment of $33 million. All notice, distribution, and administration costs would be included within the class fund, subject to the agreed documentation, advance-budget, and court-approval safeguards; counsel’s expenses would remain within the fee amount. Distribution would be automatic, with no claims requirement or class-fund reversion. Residuals would first support further distributions where economically feasible, followed by a court-approved process benefiting the class. Brightline may oppose the fee request, and any unawarded fees would augment the class fund rather than reduce Brightline’s total commitment. This is a further $2 million concession while preserving meaningful recovery for the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate your further concession. The remaining valuation gap is narrowing, and we propose a $28 million class fund plus up to $3 million for court-approved attorneys’ fees and counsel’s expenses, for an aggregate Brightline commitment of $31 million, inclusive of all settlement costs. We retain the agreed protections: automatic distribution without a claims requirement; no class-fund reversion; reasonable, documented notice and administration costs within the class fund, subject to an advance budget disclosed to both sides and court approval; and residuals used first for further distributions where economically feasible, then through a court-approved process benefiting the class. Brightline may oppose the fee request, and all unawarded fees would augment the class fund. This further increase provides substantial, prompt recovery while reflecting the remaining certification and litigation risks.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose resolving the remaining valuation gap at a $29 million class fund plus $3 million allocated to court-approved attorneys’ fees and counsel’s expenses, for a fixed aggregate commitment of $32 million inclusive of all settlement costs. All previously agreed protections remain: automatic payments without a claims requirement; no class-fund reversion; reasonable, documented notice, distribution, and administration costs within the class fund, subject to an advance budget disclosed to both sides and court approval; and residuals directed first to further distributions where economically feasible, then to a court-approved process benefiting the class. Brightline may oppose the fee request. Any unawarded fees augment the class fund and do not reduce the $32 million commitment. This midpoint resolves the remaining monetary difference while preserving prompt, meaningful class relief.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline accepts your latest term sheet: a $29 million class fund and $3 million allocated to court-approved attorneys’ fees and counsel’s expenses, for a fixed $32 million aggregate commitment inclusive of all settlement costs. Acceptance includes the administration safeguards and residual-distribution sequence stated in your message, automatic payments without a claims requirement, and no class-fund reversion. Brightline retains the right to oppose the fee request; any unawarded fees augment the class fund without reducing the aggregate commitment. We have a binding agreement for submission to the court for approval and can proceed to settlement documentation and the approval papers.

The opening demand totals $39.5 million, within authority but leaves little room for administration and offers no cost savings through negotiation. Counter materially lower while preserving automatic distribution and independent fee review, which support approval. Do not disclose the ceiling. Clarify that administration must fit within the stated fund and fee expenses within the fee cap.

The defense offer provides substantial certain recovery, but there is room to negotiate a higher class fund. Preserve automatic distribution and nonreversion while reducing the fee request rather than protecting foundation reimbursement at the class’s expense. Administration costs should be reasonable and supervised so the headline fund translates into meaningful payments.

Their reduction to $35 million total leaves room to negotiate further below the authorized ceiling. Counter at $30 million total while maintaining approval-friendly automatic distribution, nonreversion, and independent fee review. Accept their administration safeguards but make the all-inclusive payment limit explicit.

The latest offer provides substantial certain recovery, but further movement is worth pursuing with three rounds remaining. Maintain the agreed distribution protections and reduce the class-fund demand by $2 million without increasing fees.

Their $33 million proposal is within authority and retains approval-friendly protections, but further negotiated savings appear achievable with three rounds remaining. Increase the class fund by $1 million, preserving all agreed safeguards and the $3 million fee ceiling. Do not disclose the authorized maximum or characterize this offer as final.

The latest offer provides substantial certain recovery despite certification risk and trial delay. With two further rounds available and a narrowing gap, a $1 million concession seeks additional class recovery while preserving the agreed protections. Fees remain subject to independent court review, with denied amounts benefiting the class.

The $32 million all-inclusive midpoint is within authority and reflects substantial negotiated reductions. Automatic distribution, nonreversion, and independent fee review support approval. Accepting secures resolution rather than risking an otherwise favorable agreement for a marginal further reduction.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement:
Hargrove Lane LLP, court-appointed interim class counsel, submits this statement in support of preliminary approval under Rule 23(e). Counsel negotiated the settlement directly with defense counsel through confidential mediation communications. This statement does not disclose confidential offers, counteroffers, or litigation assessments, and counsel does not represent that attorneys’ fees were discussed only after class relief was agreed.

The resulting agreement provides a $29 million class fund and a separate $3 million allocation for attorneys’ fees and counsel’s expenses, subject to court approval. Brightline’s aggregate commitment is fixed at $32 million. Brightline retains the right to oppose the fee request, and any fees not awarded will augment the class fund rather than revert to Brightline. The firm receives fixed compensation under a foundation-funded engagement, regardless of the outcome; any settlement fee award is payable to the foundation and does not increase the firm’s compensation.

Class members will receive payments automatically using Brightline’s existing records, without submitting claims. Reasonable, documented notice, distribution, and administration costs will be paid from the class fund, subject to an advance budget and court approval. Accordingly, the $29 million fund is not a representation of net payments to members. No class funds will revert to Brightline. Residual funds will first support additional distributions where economically feasible, with any remaining balance handled through a court-approved process benefiting the class.

Counsel considers the settlement fair, reasonable, and adequate in light of the substantial monetary relief, automatic distribution, nonreversion protections, and independent judicial review of fees. The class fund represents approximately 45% of the $64 million in disputed renewal charges before administration costs and any augmentation from unawarded fees. Although the action survived a motion to dismiss, certification remains unresolved, success on the merits is uncertain, and trial would be approximately two to three years away. Settlement avoids those risks and delays while securing substantial recovery.

Counsel requests preliminary approval and authorization of appropriate class notice. The approval submissions should provide the proposed allocation methodology, administration budget, notice plan, and information supporting settlement-class certification so the Court can assess equitable treatment among class members and the applicable Rule 23 requirements. Final approval and any fee award remain subject to the Court’s independent review and class members’ opportunity to object.
